cwe_name: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

exact_cwe_mechanism.evidence: User-controlled commit message flows through string replacement and escaping, then gets embedded in shell commands via child_process.exec() at lines 59 and 64

connection.evidence: message parameter from user-provided options flows directly to git commit and tag commands: message → escapeQuotes() → string concatenation → exec()

diff_causality.evidence: This line is the primary transformation point where user input gets processed before shell command construction. Reverting would remove the escaping attempt, leaving raw user input in shell commands

security_control.evidence: escapeQuotes function attempts to escape ["'$`\] characters but may be incomplete for OS command injection context
security_control.required_control: Complete neutralization of shell metacharacters for command injection prevention
security_control.control_requirement_evidence: CWE-78 requires proper neutralization when embedding user input in shell commands via string concatenation
existing_controls_checked: escapeQuotes function with limited character escaping
no upstream validation of commitMessage content
security_control.deficiency_evidence: escapeQuotes only escapes 5 specific characters; many shell metacharacters like ;, &, |, >, <, (, ), {, } remain unescaped and could modify command structure

concrete_impact.evidence: Potential arbitrary command execution if attacker controls commit message and can bypass limited escaping

diff_counterfactual: If the candidate line were reverted, user-controlled commit message would flow directly into shell commands without any escaping attempt, making command injection more straightforward
supporting_evidence: child_process.exec() used with string concatenation at lines 59 and 64
escapeQuotes function demonstrates awareness of shell injection risk but provides incomplete protection
User input flows from options.commitMessage through multiple layers to shell command
unresolved_facts: Whether git command execution context provides additional safety mechanisms
Exact validation and constraints on options.commitMessage parameter upstream
Whether other shell metacharacters beyond those escaped could be exploited in this specific git command context
review_comment: The commit message undergoes limited escaping before being embedded in git shell commands via string concatenation. While escapeQuotes handles some dangerous characters, it leaves many shell metacharacters unescaped, creating potential command injection risk. Replace string concatenation with parameterized command execution using child_process.execFile() or similar APIs that separate commands from arguments.
